messages.subject: ggplot+geom_point :  legend+colours
parts:
Hi!

I am new to ggplot and I am having some problems in playing with legend
+colours of point geometry.

What I want to do is to give different sizes & colour to the distance
value of each point according to n classes (in this case I have
choosen 4).

I have made this small code:

qplot(main="TITLE")+xlab("x")+ylab("y")+
geom_point(data=species,aes(species$x,species$y,size=species
$dist,colour=species$dist))+
scale_size(name="Distance to Water")+
scale_colour_gradientn(name = "Distance to Water", colours =
rainbow(4))

The data is data.frame with x,y and dist columns

However I would like to be able to tell him something like this
dist<1 will have colour="blue"
dist>=1 & <4 will have colour="green"
dist>=4 will have colour="red"

and the size will continue to be given by the dist value.


Thanks in advance!

messages.subject: Re: ggplot+geom_point :  legend+colours
parts:
Hi Silva -

It is hard to see exactly what you want because I can't reproduce your example (see the github website at the bottom of this article).  Trying to remake your data, I think what you are looking for is something like

species <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10, dist = 1:10)  

qplot(x, y, data = species, size= dist, colour = dist) +
  scale_size('Distance to Water') +
  scale_colour_gradientn('Distance to Water', colours = rainbow(4)) +
  opts(title = 'Title')

# add new variable to data frame
species$distClass <- 0  
species <- within(species,{
  distClass[dist < 3] <- 'Class 1'
  distClass[3<= dist & dist < 7] <- 'Class 2'
  distClass[dist >= 7] <- 'Class 3'  
})

# make new plot
qplot(x, y, data = species, size= distClass, colour = distClass) +
  labs(size = 'Distance to Water', colour = 'Distance to Water')
  opts(title = 'Title')

Does that help?
david.

messages.subject: RE: ggplot+geom_point :  legend+colours
parts:
Hi Silva,

May be you can do this.

Create a new group variable, say 'x' in your dataframe with values as
dist<1 = a
dist>=1 & <4 = b
dist>=4 = c

and map the variable to colour in defining aes as

geom_point(data=species,aes(species$x,species$y,size=species$dist,colour=spe
cies$x))

This will have different colours to different desired groups of dist.

Now if you want specific colours, you can use something like
> colours = c(a = 'blue', b = 'green', c = 'red')
and use
> scale_colour_manual(value = colours)

for details you can check ?scale_colour_manual

Hope this helps, Rgds,

S.N.V. Krishna
